name: Question 20
problem: Compute the rate of change of the function $f(x,y)=\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-y)$ with respect to $t$ along the curve $r(t)=⟨2\sqrt{t},4t⟩$ at the point $t=1.$
worked_solution:
The rate of change of $f(x,y,z)$ with respect to $t$ along the curve $r(t)$ is given by $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))].$ To calculate this, we can use the chain rule.

The chain rule in vector form states that

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))]=∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t).
$$

First, we need to compute $∇f(x,y):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y) & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂x}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-y)),\frac{∂}{∂y}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-y))⟩ \\  & =⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡(x-y),-\operatorname{cos}⁡(x-y)⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute $x=2\sqrt{t}$ and $y=4t$ into the above to find $∇f(r(t)):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(r(t)) & =⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\sqrt{t}-4t),-\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\sqrt{t}-4t)⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the derivative of $r(t),$ which is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2\sqrt{t}),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4t)⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{1}{\sqrt{t}},4⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))] & =∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) \\  & =⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\sqrt{t}-4t),-\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\sqrt{t}-4t)⟩\cdot ⟨\frac{1}{\sqrt{t}},4⟩ \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\sqrt{t}-4t)\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{t}}-\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\sqrt{t}-4t)\cdot 4 \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\sqrt{t}-4t)(\frac{1}{\sqrt{t}}-4).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the rate of change of $f$ along the curve $r(t)$ at $t=1$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(1))] & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\sqrt{1}-4\cdot 1)(\frac{1}{\sqrt{1}}-4) \\  & =-3\operatorname{cos}⁡2.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 20
?

Compute the rate of change of the function f(x,y)=sin⁡(x−y) with respect to t along the curve r(t)=⟨2t,4t⟩ at the point t=1.

a
−3cos⁡2
b
5cos⁡2
c
−3cos⁡8
d
0
e
cos⁡2
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The rate of change of f(x,y,z) with respect to t along the curve r(t) is given by ddt[f(r(t))]. To calculate this, we can use the chain rule.

The chain rule in vector form states that ddt[f(r(t))]=∇f(r(t))⋅r′(t).

First, we need to compute ∇f(x,y): ∇f(x,y)=⟨∂∂x(sin⁡(x−y)),∂∂y(sin⁡(x−y))⟩=⟨cos⁡(x−y),−cos⁡(x−y)⟩

Next, we substitute x=2t and y=4t into the above to find ∇f(r(t)): ∇f(r(t))=⟨cos⁡(2t−4t),−cos⁡(2t−4t)⟩

Now, we calculate the derivative of r(t), which is r′(t)=⟨ddt(2t),ddt(4t)⟩=⟨1t,4⟩.

Applying the chain rule, we get ddt[f(r(t))]=∇f(r(t))⋅r′(t)=⟨cos⁡(2t−4t),−cos⁡(2t−4t)⟩⋅⟨1t,4⟩=cos⁡(2t−4t)⋅1t−cos⁡(2t−4t)⋅4=cos⁡(2t−4t)(1t−4).

Therefore, the rate of change of f along the curve r(t) at t=1 is ddt[f(r(1))]=cos⁡(21−4⋅1)(11−4)=−3cos⁡2.
